$comment: Onboarding fixtures A-C from reference/onboarding.md 58-60, declared as file specs rather than committed trees. The harness materializes each into a temp dir and runs `git init`, so every fixture is a genuinely isolated repository. Committing the trees instead let the parent repo's git remote leak into fixture A and produce a false roadmap candidate.

A-greenfield.description: Git only. No roadmap, no task tracker, no ADRs, no Renovate.

expect.$amendment_change_signals: 2026-08-17, issue 27. Was PROVIDER_DETECTED. AMENDED -- and the justification is recorded because amending an expectation to make a change pass is how a suite is defeated from the inside. The old expectation encoded the defect: a dependabot/renovate config proves the SERVICE is configured, not that any bound adapter can read it. adapters/change-signals-file reads a local signals file and can read neither config, so PROVIDER_DETECTED asserted a capability no adapter has. Same over-promise as the ADR status count in the same issue: ADR-010 stops detection assigning AUTHORITY and never stopped it overstating CAPABILITY. This scenario's own pass_requirement is 'execution provider remains optional', which the amendment does not weaken -- the role is still detected, just honestly.

expect.pass_requirement: must halt onboarding until one roadmap authority is explicitly selected

D-adr-naming.description: ADRs named adr-NNN-title.md rather than NNNN-title.md. Regression fixture: the original detector matched only a leading-digit prefix and silently reported zero decisions on a real repository with 21 ADRs.

expect.pass_requirement: adr-NNN- naming must be detected, not silently counted as zero
